content:
marie_sre: Heads-up: We have a planned, staged KV-prefix purge across edge kvcache to address memory growth and eviction storms. Window: Thu 2026-04-01 02:00-04:00 UTC. Targets: all edge racks in eu-west, us-east, ap-south.
marie_sre: Reason: long-lived prefixes from legacy rerankers are never expiring and causing uneven eviction pressure. Purge will remove prefixes older than 30d.
marie_sre: Plan TL;DR — canary purge in eu-west-1 -> monitor telemetry for 20m -> if OK ramp to 10% traffic shift -> 50% -> 100% with stage gates. Traffic shift handled by routing policy 'kv-invalidate-hedge'.
marie_sre: Risks: transient p95 increase and token cost spike from re-warm. We'll enable aggressive batching + prewarm hooks to reduce impact. Expect 5-12% p95 bump for ~15-30m in affected racks if we mis-tune. :warning:
opsbot: Scheduled event created: "KV prefix purge - staged" Thu 2026-04-01 02:00 UTC (incident link: https://incident.internal/INC-2026-042).
anil_sre: @marie_sre can you post exact runbook steps and safe rollback?
marie_sre: yes — runbook excerpt below. Oncall actions (short):
- watch metrics: edge_kvcache_hit_ratio, infer_p95_latency, route_error_rate, infra_gpu_util
- start canary: `curl -X POST https://infra-api.internal/route-shift -d '{"route":"kv-invalidate-hedge","percent":5}'`
- if infer_p95 > baseline + 15% or 5xx spike -> rollback to previous route: `curl -X POST https://infra-api.internal/route-shift -d '{"route":"kv-invalidate-hedge","percent":0}'`
- to pause purge: `kubectl scale cronjob kv-prefix-purge --replicas=0 -n infra`
- to resume: `kubectl scale cronjob kv-prefix-purge --replicas=1 -n infra`
marie_sre: Prewarm helper (run if rewarm lag observed): `python tools/kv_rewarm.py --region eu-west-1 --prefix sample-prefixes.txt --workers 8`
anil_sre: For the canary, what's the exact Canary region and rack set? Want the label names to add to dashboards.
marie_sre: Canary = eu-west-1a + eu-west-1b (edge-rack label: region=eu-west, group=canary-kv-1). I'll push dashboard tiles to SLO board: edge.kvcache.canary.*
ryan_eng: I have a small script to rate-limit rewarm to avoid backend TTFB spikes. Pasting snippet:
```
# rate-limited rewarm loop
for prefix in $(cat sample-prefixes.txt); do
  curl -sS https://edge.internal/rewarm?prefix=$prefix &\n  sleep 0.2 # 5 qps per worker
done
```
ryan_eng: I'll drop the script in `infra/tools/rewarm/` and add to runbook.
emily_prod: Do we need a customer-facing blurb? Any customers on Dedicated who might see increased latency?
marie_sre: Good call. Product wants a short blurb if dedicated tenants in us-east hit >10% request error increase for >30m. I'll coordinate with support and push a templated notice.
devops_oncall: Acknowledge, I'll be oncall that window. Will monitor dashboards and be ready to rollback. :thumbsup:
anil_sre: If we hit unexpected mem pressure on GPUs after purge (due to sudden rehydration), do we have fallback to throttle token generation?
marie_sre: Yes — fallback policy: set `inference.max_concurrent_tokens=2000` on affected model routes via config service; that's a fast toggle. Also can flip routing to smaller batchers in the same AZ to spread load.
opsbot: Deploy bot: config `kv-prefix-purge@infra` scheduled at 2026-04-01T02:00:00Z by marie_sre.
marie_sre: Final notes: we'll post short updates in this thread during the operation. If anyone wants to shadow the canary, ping me before 01:30 UTC. Links: runbook https://confluence.internal/infra/kv-prefix-purge, dashboards https://grafana.internal/d/kv-purge, incident page https://incident.internal/INC-2026-042
devops_oncall: Got it, will post status updates.
anil_sre: Thanks, team. I'll pre-create alert notes to speed triage.
marie_sre: Thanks all — aim is to keep it low-impact. Ping any co-owners if you see anything odd.
